instruction: `JsonWriter.value(...)` (com.google.gson.stream) is overloaded seven ways, and which JSON type a call writes depends on Java overload resolution of its argument (an `int` silently goes to `value(long)`, an `Integer` to `value(Number)`, a `String` that is null writes `null`). Replace the overloads with type-named methods: `value(String)` becomes `stringValue(String)`; `value(boolean)` and `value(Boolean)` become `booleanValue(boolean)` and `booleanValue(Boolean)`; `value(float)`, `value(double)`, `value(long)` and `value(Number)` become `numberValue(float)`, `numberValue(double)`, `numberValue(long)` and `numberValue(Number)`. Bodies, annotations and Javadoc stay the same; `jsonValue(String)` and `nullValue()` are unchanged. Rename them in `JsonWriter` and in every subclass that overrides them (e.g. `com.google.gson.internal.bind.JsonTreeWriter`), and update every call of the old `value(...)` methods in every Maven module (gson, extras, proto, metrics, test-graal-native-image, test-shrinker, test-jpms), main and test code, so that each call keeps writing exactly what it wrote before: choose the new name from the static type of the argument (a `String` expression -> `stringValue`, `boolean`/`Boolean` -> `booleanValue`, any primitive number, `char` or `Number` subtype -> `numberValue`). Do not keep any `value(...)` method on `JsonWriter`, and do not touch unrelated methods named `value` (e.g. annotation `value()` elements). Behavior must not change.
